answer: A lantern is the only light an identity may act by, and the lanterns it holds must sit in meadows that share no delta and have never before lit its line. The ledger counts every identity under a root, so a fork inherits its parent's tally and each new identity needs one more meadow than the last. A newcomer needs two lamp-bearers; a holder of a thousand needs half a million unrelated sponsors, each locking capital he never withdraws.
